headline: Defense contracts grow. Startups flourish. Space diplomacy expands.
deck: Military budgets remain a solid revenue source while funding rounds surge for space startups.

stories.head: Viasat secures $307M for Marine Corps comms
stories.body: Viasat has landed a $307 million contract to provide satellite communications for the Marine Corps, reaffirming that defense budgets are a steady business model. This deal highlights the enduring appeal of military contracts for tech firms, especially as other sectors face uncertainty.
stories.soWhat: If you're looking for reliable revenue, the military seems to be the safest bet in town.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully raised $190 million in a Series C funding round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding will bolster its capabilities in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, indicating that the DoD's appetite for these services is growing.
stories.soWhat: In a world where revenue often trumps innovation, True Anomaly's success underscores the military's growing reliance on commercial space solutions.

stories.head: Paraguay signs Artemis Accords, joins space club
stories.body: Paraguay has officially signed the Artemis Accords, becoming the sixth nation to do so recently. This move suggests that space diplomacy is becoming a key component of international relations, as countries jockey for position in the new frontier.
stories.soWhat: If space is the new geopolitical battleground, then signing these accords is like getting a VIP pass to the after-party.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Rocket Lab's acquisition plans
watchlist.body: Rocket Lab's intention to acquire a space robotics company could signal a shift in their strategic focus, potentially reshaping their launch capabilities.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests continue to delay
watchlist.body: With another delay in hypersonic tests, the credibility of this program is increasingly in question; investors will be watching closely.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser faces scrutiny
watchlist.body: After passing its critical design review, the pressure is on Sierra Space to deliver, as stakeholders want more than just passing grades.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension may indicate defense trends
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension on the TITAN program suggests that defense contractors are prioritizing data solutions, which could set the stage for future contracts.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
